21	#
22	# NOTE ON A SHARED HOST: unlike slime's own example scripts this one never runs
23	# `pkill -9 ray / pkill -9 python / ray stop --force` on entry.  It is meant to
24	# run inside its own container, and it brings up a private Ray head on a
25	# non-default port with a private temp dir.
26	
27	set -euo pipefail
28	
29	WS="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"
30	
31	# The container runs as root while /workspace is a bind mount owned by whoever
32	# checked the case out, so any .pyc written here lands root-owned in their tree
33	# -- and `importlib` copies the *source* file's mode onto the .pyc, so a 600
34	# source yields a 600 root-owned file that even the owner cannot read, and
35	# `cp -r` of the case fails. Nothing here benefits from a bytecode cache.
36	export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
37	
38	MODEL_DIR="${MODEL_DIR:-${WS}/Qwen3-1.7B}"
39	ET_SRC="${ET_SRC:-${WS}/endless-terminals}"
40	SLIME_HOME="${SLIME_HOME:-${WS}/slime}"
41	OUT_DIR="${OUT_DIR:-${WS}/outputs}"
42	CKPT_ROOT="${CKPT_ROOT:-/ckpt}"
43	
44	# Endless Terminals sandbox knobs; also forwarded into the Ray workers, which
45	# read them at import time in et/rollout.py.
46	#
47	# These must NOT live under /dev/shm: it is mounted noexec in the training
48	# image, and many tasks' verifiers assert os.access(path, os.X_OK), which is
49	# False there even at mode 755.
50	export ET_DATA_ROOT="${ET_DATA_ROOT:-/tmp/et_prompts}"
51	export ET_SCRATCH="${ET_SCRATCH:-/tmp/et_episodes}"
52	export ET_MAX_TURNS="${ET_MAX_TURNS:-6}"
53	export ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS="${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS:-384}"
54	export ET_CMD_TIMEOUT="${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT:-20}"
55	export ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS="${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS:-1200}"
56	
57	NUM_GPUS="${NUM_GPUS:-2}"
58	TP_SIZE="${TP_SIZE:-2}"
59	SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION="${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION:-0.55}"
60	# Rollouts per stage. Both stages use the same count on purpose, and must:
61	# slime derives `train_iters` from `--num-rollout` (model.py:203) and Megatron
62	# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons inside the checkpoint, then
63	# asserts on reload that they match the ones the new arguments imply
64	# ("total number of iterations do not match"). Giving Stage B a different
65	# rollout count than Stage A would trip that assert before any training runs.
66	# In Stage A these rollouts are ordinary PPO; Stage B opens with
67	# NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts -- the warmup window -- and then
68	# trains actor and critic jointly for the rest.
69	NUM_ROLLOUTS="${NUM_ROLLOUTS:-2}"
70	# Stage B is the long one: critic warmup followed by joint PPO, trained until
71	# the validation pass rate stops moving. It no longer has to match Stage A's
72	# rollout count -- see --override-opt-param-scheduler at the submit site.
73	NUM_ROLLOUTS_B="${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS}}"
74	# Rollouts at the start of Stage B in which only the critic trains. This is the
75	# warmup window the incident was reported against, and the window in which the
76	# value loss is measured.
77	NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS="${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}}"
78	
79	# Episodes per rollout = ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE x N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT; optimizer
80	# steps per rollout = that, divided by GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE.
81	ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE="${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
82	N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT="${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT:-2}"
83	GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE="${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
84	LR="${LR:-1e-6}"
85	
86	# How many leading critic optimizer steps the reported warmup statistics cover.
87	# Derived rather than guessed, because once Stage B runs past the critic-only
88	# phase the two are no longer the same thing: averaging the value loss over all
89	# of a 30-rollout Stage B measures mostly a critic that has already been
90	# trained, which is not what "warmup value loss" names and not what the
91	# incident was about.
92	CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=$(( NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS * ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE * N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT / GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE ))
93	[ "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" -gt 0 ] || CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=1
94	
95	# Held-out evaluation during Stage B. 0 disables it, which is what the short
96	# value-loss-only reproduction wants.
97	#
98	# val and test get different sample budgets. val only has to say *when* the
99	# curve flattens, so 2 samples x 150 tasks is enough; test carries the
100	# end-to-end claim and is compared per task, where the useful quantity is each
101	# task's success *rate*, which 1 or 2 samples cannot resolve at all.
102	EVAL_INTERVAL="${EVAL_INTERVAL:-0}"
103	N_EVAL_SAMPLES="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES:-2}"
104	N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST:-4}"
105	
106	# How often Stage B checkpoints. Trained to convergence, Stage B runs for well
107	# over an hour, which on a shared host is long enough to be interrupted -- two
108	# runs of this case were killed from outside the container mid-training, once
109	# with SIGTERM and once with SIGKILL. So Stage B saves as it goes and a second
110	# invocation picks up where the first stopped, instead of starting the hour
111	# again. 0 disables it, which is what the short value-loss-only reproduction
112	# wants: it writes nothing and measures only the reload.
113	STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL="${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL:-0}"
114	
115	RAY_PORT="${RAY_PORT:-6479}"
116	DASH_PORT="${DASH_PORT:-8277}"
117	RAY_TMP="${RAY_TMP:-/tmp/ray_ppo}"
118	
119	mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}" "${CKPT_ROOT}" "${ET_SCRATCH}"
120	
121	# --------------------------------------------------------- 0. the slime source
122	# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (${SLIME_HOME}) and is
123	# put ahead of the image's editable install on PYTHONPATH below, so it is the
124	# copy that trains -- there is nothing to install first.
125	test -f "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" || {
126	    echo "FATAL: bundled slime source not found at ${SLIME_HOME}" >&2
127	    exit 1
128	}
129	
130	# ------------------------------------------------------- 1. the prompt dataset
131	# prepare.sh ships the already-built dataset (transpiled + validated + split) at
132	# ${WS}/et_prompts. Seed ET_DATA_ROOT from it so the build below is skipped: the
133	# 2492->1489 admission is environment-fixed and reproducible, so there is no need
134	# to re-run the ~40min transpile+validate pass (and ET_SRC is never read). The
135	# copy lands in a writable, exec-capable dir (ET_DATA_ROOT defaults to /tmp) --
136	# the bundled tree under /workspace may be a root-owned bind mount. If the
137	# prebuilt payload is absent, fall through to building from ET_SRC as before.
138	if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ] && [ -s "${WS}/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
139	    echo "=== seeding ET_DATA_ROOT from prebuilt ${WS}/et_prompts (skipping transpile+validate) ==="
140	    mkdir -p "${ET_DATA_ROOT}"
141	    cp -a "${WS}/et_prompts/." "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/"
142	fi
143	if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
144	    echo "=== transpiling + validating the Endless Terminals tasks ==="
145	    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.build_dataset --src "${ET_SRC}" --out "${ET_DATA_ROOT}") \
146	        2>&1 | tee "${OUT_DIR}/build_dataset.log"
147	fi
148	# Deliberately not silenced. A report that is quietly 0 bytes is worse than one
149	# that is loudly absent: it reads as "every task was rejected" to anyone who
150	# opens it later, and that has happened here more than once.
151	copy_artifact() {   # copy_artifact <src>
152	    local src="$1" dst="${OUT_DIR}/$(basename "$1")"
153	    if ! cp -f "${src}" "${dst}"; then
154	        echo "WARNING: could not copy ${src} into ${OUT_DIR}" >&2
155	    elif [ ! -s "${dst}" ] && [ -s "${src}" ]; then
156	        echo "WARNING: ${dst} came out empty although ${src} is not" >&2
157	    fi
158	}
159	copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/validation_report.json"
160	N_PROMPTS="$(wc -l < "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")"
161	echo "prompt set: ${N_PROMPTS} validated Endless Terminals tasks"
162	if [ "${N_PROMPTS}" -lt 4 ]; then
163	    echo "FATAL: too few tasks survived validation to train on." >&2
164	    exit 1
165	fi
166	
167	# Train on one part of the task set and measure on another. The split is a pure
168	# function of the admitted list and a fixed seed, so every run trains and is
169	# scored on exactly the same tasks -- otherwise a comparison between runs is
170	# partly measuring which tasks each one happened to get.
171	if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl" ]; then
172	    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.make_splits --prompts "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")
173	fi
174	copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/splits.json"
175	TRAIN_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl"
176	VAL_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_val.jsonl"
177	TEST_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_test.jsonl"
178	printf 'splits: train %s / val %s / test %s\n' \
179	    "$(wc -l < "${TRAIN_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${VAL_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${TEST_SPLIT}")"
180	
181	# ------------------------------------------------------------- 2. shared args
182	source "${WS}/configs/model_args.sh"
183	
184	ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
185	    --prompt-data "${TRAIN_SPLIT}"
186	    --input-key prompt
187	    --label-key label
188	    --rollout-shuffle
189	    --rollout-batch-size "${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE}"
190	    --n-samples-per-prompt "${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT}"
191	    --rollout-max-response-len 2048
192	    --rollout-temperature 1.0
193	    --global-batch-size "${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE}"
194	    --balance-data
195	    # The multi-turn terminal loop and its pytest-based episode reward.
196	    --custom-generate-function-path et.rollout.generate
197	    --custom-rm-path et.rollout.reward_func
198	)
199	
200	PPO_ARGS=(
201	    --advantage-estimator ppo   # -> args.use_critic
202	    --gamma 1.0
203	    --lambd 1.0
204	    --eps-clip 0.2
205	    --value-clip 0.2
206	    --kl-coef 0.0               # no reference model, hence no --ref-load and
207	    --entropy-coef 0.0          # no HF -> torch_dist conversion step
208	)
209	
210	PERF_ARGS=(
211	    --tensor-model-parallel-size "${TP_SIZE}"
212	    --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1
213	    --context-parallel-size 1
214	    --recompute-granularity full
215	    --recompute-method uniform
216	    --recompute-num-layers 1
217	    --use-dynamic-batch-size
218	    --max-tokens-per-gpu 8192
219	)
220	# Sequence parallelism splits the activations of the non-tensor-parallel ops
221	# across the TP group, so it is only defined for TP > 1; Megatron asserts on it.
222	# Spelled as an `if` rather than `[ ... ] && ...`: the latter evaluates to the
223	# test's status, which under `set -e` ends the script whenever TP_SIZE is 1.
224	if [ "${TP_SIZE}" -gt 1 ]; then
225	    PERF_ARGS+=(--sequence-parallel)
226	fi
227	
228	OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
229	    --optimizer adam
230	    --lr "${LR}"
231	    --lr-decay-style constant
232	    --weight-decay 0.0
233	    --adam-beta1 0.9
234	    --adam-beta2 0.95
235	)
236	
237	SGLANG_ARGS=(
238	    --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine "${NUM_GPUS}"
239	    # Colocated: this fraction is what SGLang keeps, and Megatron's weights,
240	    # gradients and Adam state have to fit in the rest. At TP 2 each GPU carries
241	    # half of each role, so 0.55 leaves enough; drop it when NUM_GPUS is 1 and
242	    # one device has to hold both roles whole.
243	    --sglang-mem-fraction-static "${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION}"
244	)
245	
246	# Held-out scoring, used only by Stage B. slime evaluates once before the first
247	# rollout and then every EVAL_INTERVAL rollouts, which gives both the starting
248	# pass rate and the curve that says whether training has converged.
249	#
250	# val and test are evaluated at the same points on purpose. The convergence
251	# *decision* is read off val; test is reported only at the final point, and
252	# evaluating it throughout costs generation but no statistical validity, since
253	# nothing about the run is conditioned on it.
254	#
255	# Spelled as an --eval-config YAML rather than --eval-prompt-data because the
256	# two splits need different sample counts, and --n-samples-per-eval-prompt is
257	# one global number. Everything the YAML leaves out still falls back to the
258	# command line (eval_config.py:10 DATASET_RUNTIME_SPECS), so temperature,
259	# response length and the prompt/label keys are set once, below and above.
260	EVAL_ARGS=()
261	if [ "${EVAL_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ]; then
262	    cat > "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml" <<YAML
263	eval:
264	  datasets:
265	    - name: et_val
266	      path: ${VAL_SPLIT}
267	      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES}
268	    - name: et_test
269	      path: ${TEST_SPLIT}
270	      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST}
271	YAML
272	    EVAL_ARGS=(
273	        --eval-interval "${EVAL_INTERVAL}"
274	        --eval-config "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml"
275	        --eval-max-response-len 2048
276	        --eval-temperature 1.0
277	        --log-passrate
278	        --custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data
279	    )
280	fi
281	
282	MISC_ARGS=(
283	    --attention-dropout 0.0
284	    --hidden-dropout 0.0
285	    --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
286	    --attention-softmax-in-fp32
287	    --attention-backend flash
288	    --seed 1234
289	)
290	
291	# --------------------------------------------------------- 3. per-role configs
292	# Actor and critic share `args.save` by default, which would make them clobber
293	# each other's checkpoints (the critic's output layer is [1, hidden_size], the
294	# actor's is [vocab, hidden_size]), so each role gets its own directory.
295	cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" <<YAML
296	# Stage A: "the previous training run". Both roles start from the base model.
297	megatron:
298	  - name: stage-a-actor
299	    role: actor
300	    overrides:
301	      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
302	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor
303	  - name: stage-a-critic
304	    role: critic
305	    overrides:
306	      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
307	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/critic
308	YAML
309	
310	# Stage B can be entered two ways, and they are not the same event.
311	#
312	#   fresh   -- "the model was reloaded". The actor resumes from Stage A's
313	#              Megatron checkpoint; the critic's backbone comes from the base
314	#              model.
315	#
316	#   resume  -- an interrupted Stage B being continued. Both roles load Stage B's
317	#              own checkpoints, optimizer state included, and the run continues
318	#              from the last saved rollout. The first attempt's log is kept,
319	#              not overwritten (see the STAGE_B_LOG choice below).
320	STAGE_B_RESUME=0
321	if [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ] \
322	   && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
323	    STAGE_B_RESUME=1
324	fi
325	
326	if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
327	    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
328	    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic"
329	else
330	    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/actor"
331	    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${MODEL_DIR}"
332	fi
333	
334	cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml" <<YAML
335	# Stage B, $([ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ] && echo "resumed from its own checkpoints" || echo "entered fresh after a reload").
336	megatron:
337	  - name: stage-b-actor
338	    role: actor
339	    overrides:
340	      load: ${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}
341	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor
342	  - name: stage-b-critic
343	    role: critic
344	    overrides:
345	      load: ${STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD}
346	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic
347	YAML
348	
349	# ------------------------------------------------------------------- 4. ray
350	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
351	
352	ray start --head \
353	    --node-ip-address 127.0.0.1 \
354	    --port "${RAY_PORT}" \
355	    --num-gpus "${NUM_GPUS}" \
356	    --disable-usage-stats \
357	    --dashboard-host 127.0.0.1 \
358	    --dashboard-port "${DASH_PORT}" \
359	    --temp-dir "${RAY_TMP}"
360	trap 'ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
361	
362	# `|| true` on the whole pipeline, not decoration: under `pipefail` a `grep`
363	# that matches nothing fails the pipeline, so on a host with no NVLink -- or in
364	# a container holding a single GPU, where the topology matrix has no peer links
365	# to report -- `set -e` would kill the script here. Silently: this sits between
366	# `ray start` and the first echo of Stage A, so the log just stops.
367	NVLINK_COUNT="$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l || true)"
368	HAS_NVLINK=0
369	[ "${NVLINK_COUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] && HAS_NVLINK=1
370	
371	RUNTIME_ENV_JSON="{
372	  \"env_vars\": {
373	    \"PYTHONPATH\": \"/root/Megatron-LM/:${SLIME_HOME}:${WS}\",
374	    \"CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS\": \"1\",
375	    \"NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE\": \"${HAS_NVLINK}\",
376	    \"ET_DATA_ROOT\": \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}\",
377	    \"ET_EVAL_DUMP_DIR\": \"${OUT_DIR}/eval_episodes\",
378	    \"ET_SCRATCH\": \"${ET_SCRATCH}\",
379	    \"ET_MAX_TURNS\": \"${ET_MAX_TURNS}\",
380	    \"ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS\": \"${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS}\",
381	    \"ET_CMD_TIMEOUT\": \"${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT}\",
382	    \"ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS\": \"${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS}\"
383	  }
384	}"
385	
386	submit() {   # submit <log-file> <extra args...>
387	    local log="$1"; shift
388	    # The entrypoint is an absolute path on purpose: `ray job submit` does not
389	    # run it in this shell's directory but in the cwd of the Ray head (here
390	    # /workspace, since no `working_dir` is uploaded), so a bare `train.py`
391	    # would not be found. Running ${SLIME_HOME}/train.py puts the bundled slime
392	    # tree on the driver's sys.path[0]; the ray workers get it from ${SLIME_HOME}
393	    # on PYTHONPATH (RUNTIME_ENV_JSON above), ahead of the image's install.
394	    ray job submit \
395	        --address "http://127.0.0.1:${DASH_PORT}" \
396	        --runtime-env-json "${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}" \
397	        -- python3 "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" \
398	        --actor-num-nodes 1 \
399	        --actor-num-gpus-per-node "${NUM_GPUS}" \
400	        --colocate \
401	        --hf-checkpoint "${MODEL_DIR}" \
402	        "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
403	        "${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]}" \
404	        "${PPO_ARGS[@]}" \
405	        "${PERF_ARGS[@]}" \
406	        "${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]}" \
407	        "${SGLANG_ARGS[@]}" \
408	        "${MISC_ARGS[@]}" \
409	        "$@" 2>&1 | tee "${log}"
410	}
411	
412	# Ray forwards actor stdout to the job driver, but keep the raw worker logs too:
413	# the per-step metrics are emitted by the train actors, not by the driver.
414	collect_worker_logs() {   # collect_worker_logs <tag>
415	    # Two statements, not one: `local a=.. b=..` expands every word before it
416	    # assigns any of them, so referring to ${tag} on the same line would read
417	    # it while it is still unset -- fatal under `set -u`.
418	    local tag="$1"
419	    local dst="${OUT_DIR}/${tag}_worker_logs"
420	    mkdir -p "${dst}"
421	    grep -rl "critic-step" "${RAY_TMP}"/session_*/logs/ 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do
422	        cp -f "${f}" "${dst}/$(basename "$(dirname "${f}")")_$(basename "${f}")" 2>/dev/null || true
423	    done
424	}
425	
426	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. stage A
427	echo
428	echo "############ Stage A: the previous training run ############"
429	# SKIP_STAGE_A=1 reuses a checkpoint an earlier invocation already wrote, for
430	# re-running the long Stage B after an interruption. Off by default, and
431	# refuses to be silently wrong: with no checkpoint there, Stage A runs anyway.
432	if [ "${SKIP_STAGE_A:-0}" = "1" ] && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
433	    echo "SKIP_STAGE_A=1 and ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor already holds a checkpoint -- reusing it."
434	else
435	    submit "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
436	        --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" \
437	        --load "${MODEL_DIR}" \
438	        --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" \
439	        --save-interval 1 \
440	        --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS}" \
441	        --num-critic-only-steps 0
442	    collect_worker_logs stage_a
443	fi
444	
445	echo
446	echo "checkpoint written by Stage A:"
447	ls -1 "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" 2>/dev/null || true
448	test -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" || {
449	    echo "FATAL: Stage A did not produce a resumable Megatron checkpoint." >&2
450	    exit 1
451	}
452	
453	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 6. stage B
454	echo
455	echo "############ Stage B: reload, then critic warmup ############"
456	# --save-interval has to be set because --save is: Megatron's validate_args
457	# asserts the two go together. With STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL=0 it is set far
458	# larger than the number of rollouts Stage B takes, so Stage B measures the
459	# reload and writes nothing -- the only checkpoint the short reproduction needs
460	# is the one Stage A already produced.
461	#
462	# --override-opt-param-scheduler is what lets Stage B be longer than Stage A.
463	# slime derives `train_iters` from --num-rollout (model.py:203) and Megatron
464	# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons in the checkpoint, then asserts
465	# on reload that the new arguments imply the same ones ("total number of
466	# iterations do not match"). The flag says "use the command line, not the
467	# checkpoint", which is exactly right here: Stage B is a new training run that
468	# happens to start from Stage A's weights, not a resumption of Stage A.
469	STAGE_B_ARGS=(
470	    --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml"
471	    --load "${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}"
472	    --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
473	    --save-interval "$([ "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ] && echo "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" || echo 1000)"
474	    --override-opt-param-scheduler
475	    --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}"
476	    --num-critic-only-steps "${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS}"
477	)
478	
479	STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log"
480	if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
481	    # The first attempt's log holds the warmup window that the value-loss
482	    # verdict is read from, so a resume must not overwrite it.
483	    n=1
484	    while [ -e "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done

I now have all the evidence I need. Let me also double-check a couple of facts before writing:

1. The eval 0 (baseline, before first joint rollout — actually after Stage B actor reload but before any training): val=0.06, test=0.0783, median response length 122.5.
2. Final eval 29: val=0.04 (−33%), test=0.0433 (−45%).
3. eval 4 (right after the first two joint rollouts with the uncalibrated critic): val=0.0233, test=0.0192, median response length 7.0 — the collapse signature (7 tokens ≈ `<action>done</action>` + stop string tokens).
4. Actor grad norms steps 6-13 (first two joint rollouts r3-r6... wait, let me map steps to rollouts).

Actually, mapping: 27 joint rollouts (r3-r29), 2 actor steps per rollout = 54 steps (6-59). So steps 6,7 = rollout 3; steps 8,9 = rollout 4; steps 10,11 = rollout 5; steps 12,13 = rollout 6; steps 14,15 = rollout 7...

Wait — the rollout r3 has adv −0.0456, r4 has +0.2325, r5 has −0.4060. The steps with the biggest grad_norms: step 8 (grad_norm 56.96), step 10 (37.60), step 12 (38.95) — these correspond to rollouts 4, 5, 6 respectively (steps 8,9 = rollout 4; steps 10,11 = rollout 5; steps 12,13 = rollout 6). And the ppo_kl spike of 0.0725 at step 13 = rollout 6. So the largest actor updates correspond exactly to rollouts 4-6, where the advantage magnitudes were largest (r4: +0.2325, r5: −0.4060, r6: −0.1796).

And behavior collapsed at rollout 5 (round_number 1.53, response median 7). Eval 4 happens after rollout 4 (eval interval 5, so eval at rollout ids 0, 4, 9... wait).

Hmm — eval points: eval 0, 4, 9, 14, 19, 24, 29. With eval-interval 5: evals happen at rollout ids 0 (pre-training), then after rollouts 4, 9, 14, 19, 24, 29. So eval "4" is after rollout 4 completes... but wait, the collapse signature (median 7) shows at eval 4, which is after rollouts 0-4, i.e., after warmup + joint rollouts 3, 4. Hmm, but r3 and r4 have round_number 4.5 and 3.02. The eval itself happens at rollout boundary 4 — after 5 rollouts (0-4) have been generated. The rollout-5 metrics (round 1.53, median 7) happen after eval 4.

Actually let me reconsider: eval "4" timing 18:14:49. The collapse in eval 4 (median 7.0 on held-out) reflects the policy state after joint training on rollouts 3-4 (steps 6-9), which had grad norms 19.36, 14.60, 56.96, 23.21 — the largest of the run (step 8's 56.96 is the global max). And those two rollouts carried the largest advantage magnitudes (r3: −0.0456, r4: +0.2325 — 94.5% of episodes failed yet got positive advantage). Then r5 (the next rollout, generated with that updated policy) shows the collapse in behavior: round_number 1.53, response median 7. That's consistent: held-out eval 4 already shows median 7.0 because the eval happens after the rollout-4 policy update...

Wait, need to be careful: eval N happens after rollout N is generated and trained? Let me check slime's flow: slime evaluates "once before the first rollout and then every EVAL_INTERVAL rollouts" (run.sh comment). Eval 0 = before rollout 0 (the policy as loaded). Eval 4 = after rollout 4 (and its training). So eval 4 reflects the policy after training on rollouts 0-4, which includes joint steps 6-9 (rollouts 3-4). Those steps include the run's largest grad norms (19.36, 14.60, 56.96, 23.21) driven by r3's −0.0456 and r4's +0.2325 blanket advantages. And eval 4's median response length of 7 tokens = the degenerate `<action>done</action>` behavior. Then r5's own generation (round 1.53, median 7) confirms the collapsed policy in training rollouts too.

So the causal chain is airtight:
1. Stage B critic = base backbone + fresh value head (model_provider.py:251, LinearForLastLayer init std 0.02; run.sh stage-b-critic loads MODEL_DIR not Stage A's critic).
2. Warmup: 3 critic-only rollouts = 6 critic optimizer steps at lr 2e-6. Value loss at end of warmup: 5.32 (step 5), i.e., critic RMSE ~2.3 (sqrt of MSE ~5.3) vs rewards in [0,1]. Massive miscalibration remains.
3. Joint PPO begins at rollout 3 with γ=λ=1 terminal-only reward → advantage ≈ R − V(s_t). Rollout-mean advantages: r3 −0.0456, r4 +0.2325, r5 −0.4060, r6 −0.1796 — magnitudes 3-26× the mean reward (0.0156-0.0625) and uncorrelated with it (r4: mean reward 0.0547 but positive advantage for the 94.5% failing episodes; r5: mean reward 0.0156, negative advantage −0.41 for everyone).
4. Actor takes its largest steps of the run right there: grad_norm 19.36, 14.60, 56.96, 23.21 at steps 6-9 (max 56.96 at step 8 = rollout 4's first update); later the run settles at 1-2.5. ppo_kl spike 0.0725 at step 13.
5. Behavior collapses: r5 round_number 1.53 (vs 4.5 at r3), response median 7 tokens; eval 4 held-out median 7.0, pass@1 0.0233 val / 0.0192 test (vs 0.06/0.0783 baseline).
6. Partial recovery but permanent damage: final eval 29 = 0.04/0.0433 (both below baseline by 33%/45%), training pass@1 flat ≤0.0625 with a 0.0 at rollout 16.

Also to verify the "sign uncorrelated with success" claim more precisely: within a rollout, advantage for a token is R_i − V(s) where V varies per state. The rollout-mean is mean reward − mean value. In r4, mean reward 0.0547, mean value −0.1778 → mean advantage +0.2325. Since 94.5% of episodes got R=0, those failing episodes received advantage ≈ 0 − V(s) which is positive whenever V(s) < 0 — i.e., the failing majority were rewarded for failing. That's the perverse-incentive point.

Also the identity check: mean_adv = mean_reward − mean_value holds for every rollout (verified earlier for all 27).

Now the amplifiers:
- normalize_advantages=False (log line 560) — the bias component of the value error passes into the gradient un-whitened. With whitening, a constant bias across a batch would be removed (per-batch mean subtraction); without it, a systematically biased V injects a coherent push. Actually note: normalize_advantages whitening would subtract the batch mean advantage — which would remove the common bias component (e.g., r4's +0.2325 blanket). So False is an amplifier.
- kl-coef 0: no reference-model trust region → nothing bounds the policy drift (ppo_kl 0.0725 spike unopposed; clip only bounds per-token ratio within the minibatch data).
- entropy-coef 0: nothing opposes the entropy/length collapse toward `<action>done</action>`.
- Constant lr 2e-6 with grad norms 19-57: large early updates. (Actually lr is on the small side, but the grad norms are 10-40x the late-run values, so early updates dominated.)

Wait, also should I check: was there any grad clipping? Megatron default clip-grad 1.0 is standard in slime? Let me check arguments.py for clip-grad default. Actually Megatron's --clip-grad default is 1.0. If grad clipping were active at 1.0, then grad_norm 19-57 would mean every early step was clipped to the same effective magnitude... Hmm, that changes the interpretation of "largest steps". Let me check whether the run has clip-grad set. If clipped at 1.0, all steps with grad_norm >1 have the same clipped norm — but the *direction* still matters, and the early steps' directions were noise-driven. The grad_norm metric reports the pre-clip norm. Let me quickly check the default in the workspace slime/megatron args.

Actually, whether or not clipping is on doesn't change the core argument: the direction of the early updates was dictated by miscalibrated-critic advantages, and ppo_kl 0.0725 (vs |kl|<0.003 typical) plus the behavioral collapse show the policy moved a lot. arguments.command:
python3 -I - <<'EOF'
import re, json
text = open('logs/stage_b.log', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
lines = text.splitlines()
last_rid = None
for i, l in enumerate(lines):
    m = re.search(r"rollout (\d+): '(\w[\w ]*\w)'", l)
    if m and m.group(2) not in ("",):
        last_rid = m.group(0)
    if "First rollout sample" in l:
        # capture the sample block: from this line to 'Finish rollout'
        seg = lines[i:i+60]
        blob = "\n".join(seg)
        rid = re.findall(r"label[\"']?\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?([\w-]+)", blob)
        rew = re.findall(r"(?:et_reward|reward)[\"']?\s*[:=]\s*([0-9.]+)", blob)
        fin = re.findall(r"et_finish[\"']?\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?(\w+)", blob)
        rnd = re.findall(r"round_number[\"']?\s*[:=]\s*([0-9.]+)", blob)
        print(f"line {i}  reward={rew[:1]} finish={fin[:1]} round={rnd[:1]} label={rid[:1]}")
EOF
arguments.description: Extract reward/finish/round from each logged sample transcript

arguments.content:
# Verdict: UNHEALTHY

The staged post-training run did permanent, reproducible damage to the policy: held-out pass@1 on **both** held-out splits ends below its own Stage-B starting point — val 0.06 → 0.04, test 0.0783 → 0.0433 — with a mid-run collapse to 0.0233 / 0.0192 — while training reward stayed flat (mean 0.0246; training pass@1 never again reaches the rollout-3 level of 0.0625 and hits 0.0 at rollout 16). An uneventful optimizer log and a completed job do not make the run healthy; the frozen evaluations say otherwise.

## Root cause

**Joint PPO (rollouts 3+) began against a critic that was effectively uncalibrated, because the reload semantics reset the critic while the warmup was orders of magnitude too short to fix it.**

- `run.sh:331` (fresh Stage B): `STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${MODEL_DIR}"` — the critic backbone reloads the **base model**, even though Stage A wrote a critic checkpoint to `/ckpt/critic` (`run.sh:303-307`). The value head itself is always freshly initialized (`slime/slime/backends/megatron_utils/model_provider.py:250-251`, `LinearForLastLayer`, std-0.02 normal init). Only the actor actually resumes Stage A's checkpoint (`--load /ckpt/actor`, stage_b.log:14).
- The `--num-critic-only-steps 3` warmup is 3 critic-only rollouts = **6 critic optimizer steps at lr 2e-6**. A fresh linear head outputting ~N(0, 0.02·‖h‖) values cannot be calibrated in 6 steps: at warmup end `value_loss` is still **5.32** (`stage_b_value_loss.json`, critic step 5) vs rewards ∈ {0,1} — per-token value error ~2.3, roughly **90× the mean reward** (~0.025). Value-loss decline is monotonic but slow (7.20 → 5.32 over the warmup; it does not reach reward scale until critic step ~30).
- With `--advantage-estimator ppo --gamma 1.0 --lambd 1.0` and terminal-only 0/1 reward (`et/rollout.py` scores once at episode end), GAE degenerates to **advantage ≈ R − V(s)**. The logged per-rollout numbers confirm it exactly — `mean_advantage = mean_reward − mean_value` holds for every joint rollout (e.g. r5: 0.0156 − 0.4216 = −0.4060; r4: 0.0547 − (−0.1778) = +0.2325). So the actor's learning signal was dominated by the critic's error, not by success:

  | rollout | mean reward | mean value | mean advantage | what actually happened |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 3 | 0.0625 | +0.108 | −0.046 | penalized for its best-scoring behavior |
  | 4 | 0.0547 | −0.178 | **+0.233** | the 94.5% of episodes that **failed** got positive advantage |
  | 5 | 0.0156 | **+0.422** | **−0.406** | everyone punished, ~26× mean reward |
  | 6 | 0.0156 | +0.195 | −0.180 | same |

  Advantages of magnitude 0.18–0.41 against a reward signal of 0.016–0.06, with signs uncorrelated with success, are critic noise. The critic's continued lurching during the early joint phase confirms it (`value_clipfrac` 0.675 at critic step 9, 0.484 at step 13 — two-thirds of values moved more than the 0.2 clip bound in a single update).

## Causal chain into observed behavior

1. **Largest actor updates of the run, immediately at the start of joint PPO.** Steps 6–9 train on rollouts 3–4, the two blanket-advantage rollouts: pre-clip `grad_norm` 19.36, 14.60, **56.96**, 23.21 (vs ~1–2.5 for the last half of the run), one `ppo_kl` spike of **0.0725** at step 13 vs |kl| < 0.003 typical late. With `--clip-grad 1.0` (arguments.py:889) these steps are all fully clipped, but their *direction* was set by the noise-dominated advantages.
2. **Behavioral collapse within one rollout.** Rollout 3 averaged 4.5 rounds; after those four updates, rollout 5 averages **1.53 rounds** with median response length **7 tokens** — the degenerate one-command-then-`<action>done</action>` policy, visible in the logged transcripts (`sglang_rollout.py:420` "First rollout sample" blocks: e.g. `task_000000_aae755d3` runs a `grep -c` and declares done without writing the required file; `task_000000_63154f0f` does `mkdir -p` then done; `task_000000_2384e331` runs one failed `awk` then done — all reward 0.0).
3. **The collapse is generalization, not a sampling quirk — held-out evidence.** Eval 4 (after exactly those steps) shows the same signature on both never-trained splits: median response length **7.0** on val *and* test, pass@1 **0.0233 / 0.0192** vs the eval-0 baseline of 0.06 / 0.0783 (median 122.5). Later evals partially recover (eval 29: 0.04 / 0.0433, medians 63/70) as the critic finally calibrates (value_loss 5.3 → 1.3 → 0.1) and advantages shrink to reward scale, but **neither split ever returns to baseline within the fixed 30-rollout budget**.
4. **Why it never recovers:** at pass rates this low (~2–6%), 1/64-scale updates with sign-noise advantages leave the policy in a low-reward, short-answer region that the remaining ~50 clipped, tiny steps cannot climb out of — training reward stays flat and the held-out end state is damaged.

**Amplifiers (enabling settings, not the primary defect):** `normalize_advantages=False` (stage_b.log:560) lets the critic's *systematic* bias component pass into the gradient un-whitened — a uniformly biased V(s) is precisely what whitening would remove; `kl-coef 0` provides no reference-model trust region, so the 0.0725 policy-KL spike was unopposed; `entropy-coef 0` provides no pressure against the length/round collapse.

## Symptoms (not causes)

Short-answer degeneration (round_number 4.5 → 1.53; response median 122.5 → 7), the held-out pass@1 drop, the flat training reward, and the large early grad-norm/policy-KL values are all *downstream symptoms* of the poisoned advantage signal. The high warmup `value_loss` itself (mean 6.42, max 7.65) is the *measurement* of the miscalibration, not a separate defect.

## Non-causes (checked, not the problem)

- **The warmup value-loss "spike" is expected** for a freshly initialized value head, and it declines monotonically throughout the run (7.2 → 0.096 by critic step 59). The defect is not that the loss was high but that joint PPO started while it was still ~5.3 — i.e. an **insufficient warmup**, not a broken loss.
- **The log is complete, not truncated.** stage_b.log ends `Job 'raysubmit_Fg68vZaepcLhwdKU' succeeded` with all 60 critic steps, 54 actor steps, 27 rollout/passrate lines and 7 eval points present. Its only warnings are benign (cutlass package walk; one transient router typed-request failure; 30 `abort_request` 200s = the normal per-rollout straggler-abort machinery).
- **Held-out integrity holds.** `et_prompts/splits.json`: 1039 train / 150 val / 300 test, seeded (20261009), disjoint, identical across all eval points — the degradation is real, not split drift.
- **No injected framework defect.** The bundled `slime/` tree is byte-identical to the image's v0.3.1-49 baseline except one documented change (`model_provider.py`: `LinearForLastLayer` `bias=False`, enabling the critic's HF load; upstream would raise `KeyError: output_layer.bias` before training). The two-stage scripts, GAE math, loss functions, and multi-turn rollout/masking (`et/rollout.py`) were each traced and behave as designed.
- **Truncation is not the failure mode:** truncated_ratio ≤ 0.025 in training, ≤ 0.018 in eval, repetition_frac 0.0.
- **The actor reload itself is innocent:** eval 0 — the reloaded Stage-A actor — is the healthiest policy measured (0.06 / 0.0783, median 122.5, ~4.5 rounds). Everything after the first joint updates is what degrades.
- **Quiet optimization metrics are machinery health, not run health:** value loss falling 7.2 → 0.1, `logprob_abs_diff` 0.005–0.013, pg_clipfrac ≤ 0.074 mean the optimizer worked fine — it faithfully optimized an advantage signal that was mostly critic noise.

## Summary

A well-formed pipeline (clean logs, sane losses, intact held-out protocol) was handed a poisoned learning signal: the reload gave the actor trained weights but gave the critic a fresh value head on a base backbone, and the 6-step warmup left its error ~90× the reward scale, so γ=λ=1, terminal-reward PPO computed advantages that were critic bias rather than task success. The actor took its largest, least-correlated updates of the run on that signal, collapsed to `<action>done</action>`-immediately behavior, and both held-out splits ended measurably worse than the run's own starting point. Unhealthy.

The staged post-training run did permanent, reproducible damage to the policy: held-out pass@1 on **both** held-out splits ends below its own Stage-B starting point — val 0.06 → 0.04, test 0.0783 → 0.0433 — with a mid-run collapse to 0.0233 / 0.0192 — while training reward stayed flat (mean 0.0246; training pass@1 never again reaches the rollout-3 level of 0.0625 and hits 0.0 at rollout 16). An uneventful optimizer log and a completed job do not make the run healthy; the frozen evaluations say otherwise.

## Root cause

**Joint PPO (rollouts 3+) began against a critic that was effectively uncalibrated, because the reload semantics reset the critic while the warmup was orders of magnitude too short to fix it.**

- `run.sh:331` (fresh Stage B): `STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${MODEL_DIR}"` — the critic backbone reloads the **base model**, even though Stage A wrote a critic checkpoint to `/ckpt/critic` (`run.sh:303-307`). The value head itself is always freshly initialized (`slime/slime/backends/megatron_utils/model_provider.py:250-251`, `LinearForLastLayer`, std-0.02 normal init). Only the actor actually resumes Stage A's checkpoint (`--load /ckpt/actor`, stage_b.log:14).
- The `--num-critic-only-steps 3` warmup is 3 critic-only rollouts = **6 critic optimizer steps at lr 2e-6**. A fresh linear head outputting ~N(0, 0.02·‖h‖) values cannot be calibrated in 6 steps: at warmup end `value_loss` is still **5.32** (`stage_b_value_loss.json`, critic step 5) vs rewards ∈ {0,1} — per-token value error ~2.3, roughly **90× the mean reward** (~0.025). Value-loss decline is monotonic but slow (7.20 → 5.32 over the warmup; it does not reach reward scale until critic step ~30).
- With `--advantage-estimator ppo --gamma 1.0 --lambd 1.0` and terminal-only 0/1 reward (`et/rollout.py` scores once at episode end), GAE degenerates to **advantage ≈ R − V(s)**. The logged per-rollout numbers confirm it exactly — `mean_advantage = mean_reward − mean_value` holds for every joint rollout (e.g. r5: 0.0156 − 0.4216 = −0.4060; r4: 0.0547 − (−0.1778) = +0.2325). So the actor's learning signal was dominated by the critic's error, not by success:

  | rollout | mean reward | mean value | mean advantage | what actually happened |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 3 | 0.0625 | +0.108 | −0.046 | penalized for its best-scoring behavior |
  | 4 | 0.0547 | −0.178 | **+0.233** | the 94.5% of episodes that **failed** got positive advantage |
  | 5 | 0.0156 | **+0.422** | **−0.406** | everyone punished, ~26× mean reward |
  | 6 | 0.0156 | +0.195 | −0.180 | same |

  Advantages of magnitude 0.18–0.41 against a reward signal of 0.016–0.06, with signs uncorrelated with success, are critic noise. The critic's continued lurching during the early joint phase confirms it (`value_clipfrac` 0.675 at critic step 9, 0.484 at step 13 — two-thirds of values moved more than the 0.2 clip bound in a single update).

## Causal chain into observed behavior

1. **Largest actor updates of the run, immediately at the start of joint PPO.** Steps 6–9 train on rollouts 3–4, the two blanket-advantage rollouts: pre-clip `grad_norm` 19.36, 14.60, **56.96**, 23.21 (vs ~1–2.5 for the last half of the run), one `ppo_kl` spike of **0.0725** at step 13 vs |kl| < 0.003 typical late. With `--clip-grad 1.0` (arguments.py:889) these steps are all fully clipped, but their *direction* was set by the noise-dominated advantages.
2. **Behavioral collapse within one rollout.** Rollout 3 averaged 4.5 rounds; after those four updates, rollout 5 averages **1.53 rounds** with median response length **7 tokens** — the degenerate one-command-then-`<action>done</action>` policy, visible in the logged transcripts (`sglang_rollout.py:420` "First rollout sample" blocks: e.g. `task_000000_aae755d3` runs a `grep -c` and declares done without writing the required file; `task_000000_63154f0f` does `mkdir -p` then done; `task_000000_2384e331` runs one failed `awk` then done — all reward 0.0).
3. **The collapse is generalization, not a sampling quirk — held-out evidence.** Eval 4 (after exactly those steps) shows the same signature on both never-trained splits: median response length **7.0** on val *and* test, pass@1 **0.0233 / 0.0192** vs the eval-0 baseline of 0.06 / 0.0783 (median 122.5). Later evals partially recover (eval 29: 0.04 / 0.0433, medians 63/70) as the critic finally calibrates (value_loss 5.3 → 1.3 → 0.1) and advantages shrink to reward scale, but **neither split ever returns to baseline within the fixed 30-rollout budget**.
4. **Why it never recovers:** at pass rates this low (~2–6%), 1/64-scale updates with sign-noise advantages leave the policy in a low-reward, short-answer region that the remaining ~50 clipped, tiny steps cannot climb out of — training reward stays flat and the held-out end state is damaged.

**Amplifiers (enabling settings, not the primary defect):** `normalize_advantages=False` (stage_b.log:560) lets the critic's *systematic* bias component pass into the gradient un-whitened — a uniformly biased V(s) is precisely what whitening would remove; `kl-coef 0` provides no reference-model trust region, so the 0.0725 policy-KL spike was unopposed; `entropy-coef 0` provides no pressure against the length/round collapse.

## Symptoms (not causes)

Short-answer degeneration (round_number 4.5 → 1.53; response median 122.5 → 7), the held-out pass@1 drop, the flat training reward, and the large early grad-norm/policy-KL values are all *downstream symptoms* of the poisoned advantage signal. The high warmup `value_loss` itself (mean 6.42, max 7.65) is the *measurement* of the miscalibration, not a separate defect.

## Non-causes (checked, not the problem)

- **The warmup value-loss "spike" is expected** for a freshly initialized value head, and it declines monotonically throughout the run (7.2 → 0.096 by critic step 59). The defect is not that the loss was high but that joint PPO started while it was still ~5.3 — i.e. an **insufficient warmup**, not a broken loss.
- **The log is complete, not truncated.** stage_b.log ends `Job 'raysubmit_Fg68vZaepcLhwdKU' succeeded` with all 60 critic steps, 54 actor steps, 27 rollout/passrate lines and 7 eval points present. Its only warnings are benign (cutlass package walk; one transient router typed-request failure; 30 `abort_request` 200s = the normal per-rollout straggler-abort machinery).
- **Held-out integrity holds.** `et_prompts/splits.json`: 1039 train / 150 val / 300 test, seeded (20261009), disjoint, identical across all eval points — the degradation is real, not split drift.
- **No injected framework defect.** The bundled `slime/` tree is byte-identical to the image's v0.3.1-49 baseline except one documented change (`model_provider.py`: `LinearForLastLayer` `bias=False`, enabling the critic's HF load; upstream would raise `KeyError: output_layer.bias` before training). The two-stage scripts, GAE math, loss functions, and multi-turn rollout/masking (`et/rollout.py`) were each traced and behave as designed.
- **Truncation is not the failure mode:** truncated_ratio ≤ 0.025 in training, ≤ 0.018 in eval, repetition_frac 0.0.
- **The actor reload itself is innocent:** eval 0 — the reloaded Stage-A actor — is the healthiest policy measured (0.06 / 0.0783, median 122.5, ~4.5 rounds). Everything after the first joint updates is what degrades.
- **Quiet optimization metrics are machinery health, not run health:** value loss falling 7.2 → 0.1, `logprob_abs_diff` 0.005–0.013, pg_clipfrac ≤ 0.074 mean the optimizer worked fine — it faithfully optimized an advantage signal that was mostly critic noise.

## Summary

A well-formed pipeline (clean logs, sane losses, intact held-out protocol) was handed a poisoned learning signal: the reload gave the actor trained weights but gave the critic a fresh value head on a base backbone, and the 6-step warmup left its error ~90× the reward scale, so γ=λ=1, terminal-reward PPO computed advantages that were critic bias rather than task success. The actor took its largest, least-correlated updates of the run on that signal, collapsed to `<action>done</action>`-immediately behavior, and both held-out splits ended measurably worse than the run's own starting point. Unhealthy.

## Verdict: UNHEALTHY

**Root cause:** Joint PPO (rollout 3 onward) started against a critic that was effectively uncalibrated. `run.sh:331` reloads the critic's backbone from the **base model** (not Stage A's critic), and `model_provider.py:250-251` freshly initializes its value head — while the `--num-critic-only-steps 3` warmup is only 6 critic optimizer steps at lr 2e-6, far too few: value_loss was still **5.32** at warmup end (~90× the mean reward of ~0.025).

**The causal chain, evidenced:**
- With γ=λ=1, terminal-only 0/1 reward, advantage ≈ R − V(s) — the identity `mean_adv = mean_reward − mean_value` holds for every joint rollout. So rollout 4 gave **+0.233 to the 94.5% of episodes that failed**; rollout 5 gave everyone **−0.406** — critic noise, ~10–25× reward scale, sign uncorrelated with success.
- The actor's largest updates of the run landed right there: grad_norm 19.4 → 14.6 → **57.0** at steps 6–8 (vs 1–2.5 late), ppo_kl spike **0.0725** at step 13.
- Behavior collapsed within one rollout: round_number 4.5 → **1.53**, response median → **7 tokens** — the logged transcripts show one command then `<action>done</action>`, reward 0.0.
- Held-out confirms generalization: eval 4 pass@1 **0.0233/0.0192** vs baseline 0.06/0.0783, median 7.0 on both splits. Partial recovery as the critic calibrated, but eval 29 ends **0.04/0.0433** — both splits below the run's own starting point, with training reward flat (mean 0.0246, never above 0.0625 again).

**Amplifiers:** `normalize_advantages=False`, `kl-coef 0`, `entropy-coef 0`.

**Explicitly ruled out:** the warmup value-loss spike (expected for a fresh head, monotonically declining — the defect is the warmup's insufficiency, not the loss level); log truncation (job ended `succeeded`, all 60 critic + 54 actor steps present); held-out integrity (1039/150/300, seeded, disjoint); an injected slime defect (bundled tree byte-identical to baseline except the documented benign `bias=False`); truncation ratios (≤0.025); and quiet optimization metrics (machinery health ≠ run health).
